OncallBot: PAGER -> P1: ap-southeast embeddings pool - KV eviction spike and regen errors detected (alerts: kv_eviction_rate > 90th pct, regen_error_rate x10)

Jules: I'm picking up primary. Observed eviction bursts starting ~22:05 UTC for embeddings-aps. Symptoms: regen timeouts causing context loss and increased retries. Affected tenants: AcmeCorp, TridentHealth (Acme higher impact). No full region outage but user-facing errors rising (~5% for those tenants).

Marta: Secondary here, standing by. I can take over at 02:00 UTC if needed. Quick Q: any KV TTL or retention toggles in ap-southeast in the last 12h? I see a normal model rollout at 18:30.

Jules: No intentional TTL flips. Hypothesis: hot traffic to a few prefixes + KV growth -> thrash. Mitigations applied so far:
- 22:15: enabled soft-prefetch on embeddings-aps (p99 writes dropped briefly)
- 22:40: rate-limited anonymous / low-priority traffic
- CS notified and customer retries coordinated

Samir: I applied a warmfix to increase capacity and raised eviction thresholds. Ops commands executed (monitoring):

```
# scale embeddings deployment and bump retention (temporary)
kubectl -n inference scale deploy embeddings-aps --replicas=4
rctl set pool embeddings-aps --kv-min-keep-seconds=120
```

Samir: Initial effect: eviction rate down ~30% in first 8m, but as traffic further concentrates it's trending back up. Propose temporary regional reroute of non-critical traffic to eu-west.

Jules: Agreed. Priya from CS - can you confirm customer SLAs and escalation path?

Priya (CS): AcmeCorp is high-priority (SLA 99.9). TridentHealth lower priority for now. I opened INC-3492 for AcmeCorp and advised client-side retry guidance; account execs notified. We'll escalate if >10% user-facing errors continue.

Marta: Handover checklist for my primary shift (start 02:00 UTC):
- Validate autoscale target reverts after steady state
- Keep rctl kv-min-keep-seconds=120 for now
- Monitor: grafana panels for embeddings-aps: kv_eviction_rate, regen_error_rate, p95_latency
- If kv_eviction_rate > 80th pct for 10m -> trigger full cache-prefetch (runbook step 3)

Jules: Ops quick notes for handoff:
- Primary: Jules (until 02:00 UTC). Secondary: Marta. Tertiary: Samir.
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/embeddings-aps (embeddings-aps / kv_eviction_rate, regen_error_rate, p95_latency)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-eviction-mitigation
- Tickets: INC-3492 (AcmeCorp), INC-3493 (TridentHealth)
- Logs: /var/logs/ops/INC-3492 (collected traces and grep-able hot-prefix entries)

Samir: Extra checks to watch:
- node host memory >85% indicates imminent evictions
- identify hot prefixes: logs | grep "prefix=" | sort | head -n 20

Jules: Current status: mitigations active. Replica scale and retention bump improved metrics but not stable. Next steps planned:
1) Gradual reroute of low-priority traffic to eu-west (cap 20%) - Marta to coordinate with routing
2) If eviction resumes, execute cache-prefetch roll (runbook step 3) - Samir ready to run
3) If customers still impacted after 30m, escalate to infra leads and consider read-only fallback for affected tenants

Marta: I'll schedule the reroute at :15 past the hour unless anyone objects. I'll prepare the revert patch to run after 30m stable.

Jules: Two operational reminders: Do not push model changes during mitigation window. Timestamp each action precisely for postmortem.

Priya (CS): I'll keep AcmeCorp updated and add comms to INC-3492 before we reroute.

Samir: Prefetch script (ops-runbook host) if needed:

```
# dry-run to validate prefetch targets
python ops/prefetch.py --pool embeddings-aps --batch-size 128 --dry-run
# remove --dry-run when ready to execute
```

Marta: Taking over primary at 02:00 UTC. My immediate watch: p95 latency and regen_error_rate. If either spikes above baseline for 10m, proceed with steps 1->3.

Jules: Handing over now. I've pushed a brief summary to Confluence under incident notes and saved logs to /var/logs/ops/INC-3492. Thanks team. :coffee:

Samir: Acknowledged. Standing by as tertiary. :eyes:

OncallBot: Thread pinned in #eng-oncall and incident timeline entry added.
